name: Bute Park
title: Ancient Trees in Cardiff's Bute Park: 8 to Find
meta_description: Behind Cardiff Castle, a London plane put at 1715 to 1771, Wales's champion tulip tree and a ginkgo that turns the Sunken Lawn gold each November.
intro: Bute Park catalogues more than 3,000 trees and counts about fifty British champions, and in 2023 volunteers still found a sweet chestnut 4.7 metres round that its records had missed. The park began as the private grounds of Cardiff Castle, on the flood plain of the Taff, and the oldest tree on our map dates from those years. A London plane at the edge of the Blackfriars site, where a medieval friary once stood, measures 612 centimetres round, which by the standard girth method puts its planting between 1715 and 1771. Cardiff's own parks record says planes near Blackfriars may date from Capability Brown's work on the Castle Green, though no source names this one. A beech a hundred metres north may be older than Old Man's Wood around it, which was still scrub in 1851. The newer arrivals gather by the Sunken Lawn, where Wales's champion tulip tree and Glamorgan's champion ginkgo stand 25 metres apart beside a dawn redwood, a species science met alive only in 1948. A Wellingtonia waits in the Blackweir woodland at the quiet northern end. Entry is free, and November turns the ginkgo gold.
